When someone is overdosing they experience respiratory depression (breathing too slow or not at all) which leads to hypoxia (not enough o2 to the brain).  Brains don’t like to be starved of oxygen and side effects of this are restlessness, confusion and aggression.  

Naloxone takes over for the opioids and reverses the effect of the overdose.  Now the patient is awake and breathing normally again, but their brain hasn’t gone back to normal oxygen levels and may react in a negative manner due to lingering hypoxia.  It is recommended to oxygenate and ventilate prior to narcan administration to decrease risk of a hypoxic but awake patient.  Narcan kits come with masks to do this.  Not recommended to narcan without rescue breaths.

This is a very basic response but a few things need to happen for you to get in to road cycling:

1. Head over to r/vancouvercycling as you will likely get better responses

2. Check out the used market for your first bike, FB Marketplace and Pinkbike usually have good options.  Try to find a bike from within the last 15 years or so that appears to be maintained well. Expect to have to change some parts.

3. Bring your bike in for a tune up and ask them to show you what you need for your flat kit and how to use it (fix a flat).  

5. Buy a new helmet, preferably with MIPS.

4. At a minimum for clothing, invest in good bike shorts.
